what: E2E selectors did not match the generated UI: getByLabel('Price') matched both the column menu button and the input, getByLabel('Name') matched more than one element, and 'Save' was used for the view update button, which is labelled 'Update'.
why: Builder guessed names; the catalog examples use icon-prefixed names and label-only lookups that are ambiguous on the list and form pages.
workaround: Changed the selectors to Update and to getByRole('textbox', { name }) with the helper names.

what: Seeding the description through the UI with Playwright fill() did not store the value; the save response timed out. Switching to pressSequentially with a delay and a blur made the test pass.
why: fill() sets the value in one step, which the React text area did not register as edits before save; the builder found it by trial.
workaround: a-seed-descriptions.spec.ts uses fill('') then pressSequentially(text) and clicks the Name field to blur.

what: Create button locator with exact regex /^Create$/ did not match the dialog button; the test waited 10 seconds and failed.
why: The accessible name of the button differs from the label used in the test.
workaround: Changed the locator to /Create$/.

what: Create-rename-delete test failed on a strict-mode violation: two grid cells named Temp Shoes from earlier failed runs.
why: The test used a fixed name and was not idempotent; leftovers from previous runs stayed in the database.
workaround: Made the name unique with Date.now() and added a cleanup of leftover Temp categories in the seed.

what: Sort-by-price test read prices from all table rows, including the 0 row and a non-selected row, so the expected order was wrong.
why: Row selector matched every row instead of the data rows.
workaround: Limited the selector to rows with aria-selected.

what: Footwear products test expected Wool socks to be absent, but the earlier data left it in the list; the test depended on state from other runs.
why: Test data is not isolated per run and the expectation assumed a clean list.
workaround: Changed the seed to remove leftovers and reran the suite; the suite then passed.

what: Seed upload through the generated binary input: setInputFiles set the file name in the textbox, but the test looked for an img inside the dialog and timed out.
why: The generated BinaryTypeInput shows the file name in a text field, not an image; the test expectation was wrong for the generated widget.
workaround: Asserted the textbox value img-SKU.png after upload.

what: Category products test found Running shoe twice (in the category view table and the product list), so the locator was ambiguous.
why: Same product shown in two grids on the page; locator was not scoped to the table.
workaround: Scoped the locator to the row and used exact name matching.

what: Variant create dialog had no SKU textbox when the builder tried to fill it; the test timed out.
why: Dialog or button naming differed from the test expectation; the create button label is Ok in the inline dialog.
workaround: Changed the locator to the Ok button and reran.

what: Seed and card tests counted 9 products instead of 8 because a Temp product left by a failed F10 run stayed in the list.
why: Tests are not isolated; leftovers of failed runs are not removed before the seed count check.
workaround: Added a cleanup of Temp products to the admin seed, like an admin would.

what: Variant test: Delete matched two buttons (page header and variants table), and the header showed Update and Cancel instead of Delete while the product had unsaved changes.
why: Generated page shows Update and Cancel in edit mode; two Delete buttons exist when a table is on the view.
workaround: Cancel first when visible, then Delete with .first(); Escape in finally to close a stray dialog.

what: F16 test creates two new Keycloak sign-ups on each run; the data grows and the lists are paged, so the expectations depend on earlier runs.
why: Each run adds customers and addresses; the test does not clean up or isolate them.
workaround: Used unique names per run and exact cell matches; logged as GAPS R7-9c.

what: The customer drawer looked squashed in the F09 1440 screenshot: labels cut to 'Pr...' and 'My...' and a tiny logo.
why: The screenshot helper resized the window and captured while the generated drawer was still animating its width, so the picture showed a mid-animation frame.
workaround: Helper waits until the logo reaches full width (settleLayout) before capturing at 1440; new drawer test checks labels and logo width.

what: Card locators matched other products whose descriptions mention the product name ('Hiking socks' matched two cards), giving strict-mode violations in the F20 tests.
why: Locator by text, not by the exact card name.
workaround: card() helper filters by the exact card-name element.

what: The F19 and F20 tests waited for dialog buttons with names Add to cart, Ok, Check out, and then Submit; the wrong button names and the dialog expectation cost several test runs.
why: Test expectations written before the generated dialog labels were known.
workaround: Button regex changed to Ok or Submit; the readable error is checked as a snackbar text.

what: The admin and shop product counts read 9 instead of 8 in the S04 and S08 tests after the F01 category test failed, probably leaving an extra product behind.
why: Inferred from the sequence of failed runs (level1 F01 failed at session:L2577); not confirmed by the builder.

what: F29 test created a product with SKU T-514769, which breaks the model pattern for SKU, so the create failed and the test failed.
why: Test built the SKU from the product name and clock digits without checking the SKU pattern in the model.
workaround: SKU now uses a TL or TT prefix with four digits from the stamp.

what: Every run of the F29 test leaves one inactive Temp tent product in the admin list, because the product with orders cannot be deleted.
why: No documented way to remove orders, so the test data cannot be cleaned up.
workaround: Logged as known; later round (R10) switched the test to a seeded product.

what: Admin F10 test clicked the page Delete button; after the generic delete was switched off the test timed out.
why: Generic delete removed by the F29 model change (deleteable=false) and the test selector was not updated.
workaround: Selector changed to the Delete product button and the Yes confirmation.

what: no-admin-data customer test failed: it read response bodies asynchronously and asserted before they were collected (expected 2, got 1).
why: Race in the test: response text is read after the assertion.
workaround: expect.poll on the body count; test passes when re-run.

what: Customer spec imported helpers from the admin Playwright package, which loaded a second copy of @playwright/test; Playwright then reported No tests found.
why: Shared helpers across actor packages are not documented as a supported pattern in the e2e docs.
workaround: Copied the needed helper functions into the customer spec.

what: After the wipe, the admin product list showed 9 products where the seed test expects 8, and paging expected 3 rows on page 2 but found 4: the stray Temp tent product from F29 test runs.
why: The F29 test left a product behind on each run (R9-16 not yet fixed).
workaround: F29 test now uses the seeded Trail backpack product and reactivates it in cleanup.

what: Test helper problems: the PDF text check failed because parentheses are escaped in the content stream; the generated date field is a group of spin-button segments, not a text box; a debug spec was used to read the DOM.
why: Test-level assumptions about PDF text and the generated date widget, not documented in writing-tests.md.
workaround: Regex escapes the parentheses; typeDate clicks the Month segment and types digits; debug spec removed after use.

what: Playwright suite failures from test design: the S11 details test opened the first product card, whose order is not fixed, and the admin 'Products' button matched two elements after the menu change.
why: Tests relied on grid order and on an ambiguous accessible name.
workaround: Opened the 'Running shoe' card by name; used an exact or specific locator.

what: Admin test for the unit dropdown flaked: Escape sometimes closes the whole dialog, so the later Back click timed out.
why: Test pressed Escape to close the option list, which also closes the dialog sometimes.
workaround: Test tolerates a closed dialog; re-run passed.

what: One integration test failed with 'Outdated instance to update' (IllegalArgumentException in the update DAO processor) after the test changed the product's stock with a stale instance.
why: Probably an instance re-read is needed after an earlier update in the same test; not confirmed against the catalog.

what: The test database is kept between runs, so tests broke on accumulated data: Wool socks ran out of stock (restocked by SQL), review, coupon and audit tables grew past one page, FK errors blocked category cleanup, and cleanup errors hid the real failure (a catch was added). F10 and F45 were flaky.
why: Round 12 is the first round that keeps data; earlier rounds wiped the DB and tests assumed an empty one.
workaround: Filter each test to its own stamp, show most rows, restock by SQL, catch cleanup errors; F10 flake fixed at the end.

what: Several Playwright assumptions were wrong: breadcrumb selected by role navigation (MUI breadcrumbs have none), a second Add-to-cart click was ignored while the first call was pending, the dashboard value was read before it loaded, and a price field showed '25.00 EUR' after blur instead of '25'.
why: Tests written against guessed DOM and timing; fixed by class selectors, waiting on responses, and checking the displayed format.
workaround: Changed selectors, awaited the POST response, asserted the displayed value.

what: Playwright checks typed 5000 into a number field that shows 5,000, and a Create button matched two elements in a dialog (strict mode).
why: Test design: the test asserted the raw value, not the formatted display; the dialog had two Create buttons.
workaround: Tests now compare the formatted value and use .last() on the dialog Create button.

what: Table pages keep every run's rows and show ten per page, so a test could not find the company or quote it had just created.
why: Test design: the tests relied on the first page of a list that grows with each run.
workaround: Tests filter by name or number with openAddAndApplyFilters.

what: Full customer suite ran with parallel workers: customers shared one cart and one seeded stock, so stock reached zero and tests interfered. Builder reset stock with a direct SQL UPDATE.
why: Test isolation: shared fixtures and parallel workers. Not a code bug.
workaround: Direct SQL reset of stock; new rule: run new spec with --grep @smoke, full suites once, serial.

what: The full customer E2E suite took 10.6 minutes at 3 workers and the admin suite 2.8 minutes. The user stopped a run as too long and asked for about 5 minutes.
why: Every round ran both full suites; no smoke subset existed.
workaround: Tagged a small @smoke set; each round runs only its new spec plus --grep @smoke; full suites run once at the end of the build.

what: With 3 workers the tests shared one customer cart and the seeded stock. Running shoe and Trail backpack dropped to 0, so add-to-cart buttons were disabled. Result: 9 customer and 3 admin failures; serial reruns passed.
why: Tests are not isolated; they depend on shared seed data and a database that is kept between runs.
workaround: Serial reruns; stock reset by a direct SQL update to the seed values.

what: The admin order lookup in the F49 test opened the all-orders table and searched the first page only. It broke once the list grew past 10 rows.
why: Test assumed the new order would be on the first page of a table that keeps every run's rows.
workaround: The test now filters the table by order number with openAddAndApplyFilters.

what: The admin clearRates helper stopped after 20 deletes, so rate rows left by earlier runs stayed and the empty-table check failed.
why: Rows accumulate across runs because the database is kept.
workaround: Loop limit raised to 60; test passed alone.

what: The shop-home test expected 8 cards; after Level 8 the sellers' published products also show, so 28 cards appeared. Builder changed the test to at least 8 without deciding the visibility rule.
why: Product visibility rule for the shop home was not decided when sellers were added.
workaround: Assertion changed to at least 8.

what: The F59 smoke test added 20 x 4.00 to the cart, which fell under the company's remaining limit after earlier orders, so no approval was requested.
why: Test depends on the state left by earlier tests and runs.
workaround: Quantity raised to 30 in the test, which is above the limit alone.

what: The F70 test expected a fixed amount due (15.90 EUR) but the cart still held the socks of a refused F69 checkout, so the value was 27.90 EUR.
why: Test assumed an empty cart; earlier failed test left items in the cart.
workaround: Test now computes amount due as total minus 1.00 paid with points.

what: A refused checkout left its dialog open, which blocked the Wallet menu click in the next step.
why: Test did not close the dialog after a refusal.
workaround: Escape pressed on both pages before the Wallet step.

what: The F69 browser test passed alone but failed in the serial level 8 run ('no balance left' not found, next step timed out) because earlier tests changed the shared cards and carts.
why: Shared state across tests in one serial file.
workaround: Test made independent by setup of its own buyer (ensureBuyer), with unique names.

what: Repeated e2e runs used up the shared seed stock (Trail shoe, Trail mix) and left about 77 products; Level 8 tests failed on out-of-stock and admin restock timed out for Trail shoe.
why: Tests shared seeded products and did not reset them.
workaround: Run-local products (see c10-09); restocked Trail mix and Wool socks through the admin UI.

what: Admin restock locator /^Stock/ matched two elements (Stock and Stock status), so the first restock script failed in strict mode.
why: Label regex too broad for the admin form.
workaround: Changed the regex to /^Stock(?! status)/.

what: Admin Products table shows 10 rows per page, so sellers' products beyond the first page are not found by the e2e helpers; a showAllRows helper selects the largest page size.
why: Default paging in the generated back-office table; the test helper assumed one page.
workaround: Added showAllRows to helpers-customer.ts and used it in adminEditProduct and level7.

what: Moving the customer menu into drop-down groups broke older specs that expected flat menu entries; clickMenu and menuCount helpers were added, and menu lookups needed retries because the menu is rebuilt after an approval.
why: Role-based locators assumed the old flat menu; the principal-driven menu changes a moment after approval.
workaround: Added MENU_GROUPS, clickMenu, menuCount and a 15-try retry loop in helpers-customer.ts.

what: The F59 smoke test depended on earlier tests having filled the cart and stock; it failed when run alone (waitForResponse on ~get timed out).
why: Order-dependent test state.
workaround: Test orders 30 units itself so it works alone.

what: The F70 refusal check expected 'You have 82 loyalty points', but the checkout was refused by the order-value rule (TOO_MANY_POINTS from CheckoutCustomImplementation.java) because the cart was worth less than the points.
why: Test chose a cart too cheap for the points rule to be the one that refuses.
workaround: Test adds a more expensive product (shops[0].product) before the 500-point attempt.

what: The F70 expiry check looked for a toast 'loyalty points expired'; the admin operation shows the message in a dialog text box.
why: Test assumed a toast; the operation's result is in a dialog field.
workaround: Assert the dialog Message textbox value, then click Back.
